title: docs(app-shell): the README flow canvas draft becomes one that saves (objectui#8854)
body:
Fixes #8854

The README's **Visual flow canvas** fence is captioned as a `flow` draft and is the block a reader pastes into the metadata admin. It could not be saved. Now it can, and a test parses it with the schema that judges it on every run.

## Three defects, one fence

Measured against the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, not against the card:

| # | Defect | Named by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `"ui": { "x": 220, "y": 180 }` — the designer's retired geometry spelling. The spec's flow node is a strict object; its canonical key is `position`, `ui` is not declared, so the node is refused by name. | objectui#8854 |
| 2 | All four edges carried only `source` / `target`. `FlowEdgeSchema` declares `id` required beside them. | objectui#8854 |
| 3 | The draft carried **no** `name` / `label` / `type`. `FlowSchema` requires all three. | nobody — found here |

Defect 3 is the reason this PR is worth reading. Repairing only the two ruled defects would have left the documented draft refused **three more times**, and the next card against this same fence would have been the third in a row.

## Which door was measured

Not the server, and not the node and edge schemas one at a time. The app-shell metadata admin validates a `flow` draft client-side by handing the **whole draft** to the spec's `FlowSchema`:

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.ts:659` — the `flow` entry in `LOADERS` loads the automation subpath's `FlowSchema`
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx:586` — `validateMetadataDraft(type, draft, …)` with the editor's entire body

The card flagged this as its own gap ("the exact call path was not measured here"). That is the measurement, and it is what surfaced defect 3: graded per node and per edge, the corrected block reports green while still being refused on save.

The block as it stood, through that real door, produces exactly **8** issues:

```
invalid_type      ["name"]            expected string, received undefined
invalid_type      ["label"]           expected string, received undefined
invalid_value     ["type"]            expected one of autolaunched|record_change|schedule|screen|api
unrecognized_keys ["nodes",1]         Unrecognized key(s) on this flow node: `ui` … keys=["ui"]
invalid_type      ["edges",0,"id"]    expected string, received undefined
invalid_type      ["edges",1,"id"]    expected string, received undefined
invalid_type      ["edges",2,"id"]    expected string, received undefined
invalid_type      ["edges",3,"id"]    expected string, received undefined
```

The corrected block: `ACCEPT`.

## What changed in the README

- `ui` becomes `position` — the same prose already documents it as requiring **both** coordinates, and that is measured true: `position` is a strict object with `x` and `y` both required.
- Each edge gains an `id` (`e1`…`e4`), matching the shape this repo's own `buildFlowSkeleton` writes.
- The draft opens with `name` / `label` / `type`, in the shape `buildFlowSkeleton` emits, under the `// flows/renewal_reminder.json` path-comment convention this same README already uses for its object draft.
- **Prose corrected in the same edit**, because a repaired block beside stale sentences is this card's defect pointed the other way:
  - a new sentence under the fence names the client-side door, so a reader knows the identity keys are part of what is validated rather than assumed;
  - the **Edges** bullet documents `id` as required and records that a bare `condition` string is widened to the ADR-0089 expression envelope on parse — measured: the parsed edge stores `"condition": { "dialect": "cel", "source": "…" }`;
  - the **Layout** bullet was re-read against the installed spec and is **unchanged**. It was already correct in every clause, including the sentence that a draft carrying `ui` is refused with a 422 — that sentence now agrees with the block above it instead of contradicting it.

## The oracle: extraction, not grepping

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts` reads the fence out of the README on every run (a hand copy drifts from the file it claims to pin), strips its jsonc comments string-aware, and parses it with `FlowSchema`. Seven cases; three of them re-inject a repaired defect into the extracted draft and require the parse to refuse it **by name**, so the green cannot come from a schema that accepts everything.

## Reverse verification — prediction stated first, then measured

Each defect was re-introduced into the committed README on disk, the file's blob hash compared against `HEAD` to prove the mutation actually landed (an editor's exit code proves nothing), the suite run, then `git checkout HEAD --` the README with the restore proved by blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| Leg | Predicted failures | Measured | Which cases went red |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` reverted to `ui` | 4 | **4** | the accept case, the `ui` control, the position case, the fence-scan case |
| the four edge `id`s removed | 2 | **2** | the accept case, the every-edge-has-an-id case |
| `name`/`label`/`type` removed | 1 | **1** | the accept case |

Prediction and result agree exactly, with no miscount to report. Restored blob `fe847122a2715b08cc6a3d020e32ddab84d2e294`, `git diff HEAD` empty, suite green again after restore (7 passed).

## Scope

- objectui#8483's one named site — the `action` to `notify` node type — is **not** revisited here. That card has already landed and its own dispatch fenced the rest of the block off; the fence still binds and no other block in this README was touched.
- Serial adjacency re-derived at start against the live open-PR list: 17 open PRs, and the app-shell README blob is byte-identical to `main` on 16 of the 17 heads. The one that differs is `changeset-release/main`, whose copy is simply older than objectui#8855 — a bot branch the release job regenerates, not work in flight.

## Verification

- New test, repo-root invocation: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts` — 7 passed, exit 0.
- Changeset gate — measured rather than assumed. `packages/app-shell/README.md` alone owes **nothing** (the gate counted it as 0 published-source files); the declaration is owed by the new test file under `src/`, which the gate counts with no test carve-out. Declared `patch` rather than empty frontmatter, following this repo's own precedent for a published README correction on a published package (`.changeset/6050-gantt-navigation-basepath.md`, `.changeset/6213-…`) — `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `files` list ships `README.md`, so published content genuinely moved. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0.
- **Full `@object-ui/app-shell` suite**, repo-root invocation under the shared verify lock: **676 test files, 6535 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0** (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, 17m12s held).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` — exit 0 (the script name is hyphenated in this package, and the run echoed it). The new test file's presence in that type-check set was proved rather than assumed: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` names it (1 hit), names a sibling flow test as a positive control (1 hit), and does not name another package's README test (0 hits).
- Repo-wide `eslint .` — **exit 0 over 4747 files, 0 errors**; the new test file is in that linted set at 0 errors / 0 warnings. This is the whole population, not a narrowing.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes` (7217 tracked text files), `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-snippets` (638/638 blocks judged), `check:doc-examples`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:readme-exports` (all 536 self-imports judged real, 0 fabricated), `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all three paths (NOT GOVERNED, with `AGENTS.md` as the lit control that shows the guard can say otherwise).
- The three build-dependent gates were red for want of a build, not for want of correctness. That was diagnosed rather than assumed: before building, `check:readme-exports` listed 13 unjudged bindings in this README and 523 more across READMEs this branch does not touch; after building the doc-gate's own scoped set, all three run clean.
- Session reference, in prose so an edit cannot strip it: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`

This pull request stays a **draft**. Landing is the maintainer's; auto-merge was not armed.
